title: Ch 3 · Exploring Diversity of Matter by its Chemical Composition

questions.q: Melamine is used to make containers because it is
questions.explain: Melamine is light, strong and can be moulded into many shapes. These properties make it a good material for containers.
questions.lo: State why knowing the chemical composition of everyday items matters (useful or harmful, recycling)

notes.0: A container that conducts heat well would get hot to hold. Melamine is chosen for properties that help it hold food and keep its shape.
notes.1: A fragile material breaks easily, which is a poor property for a container. Think about the properties a container needs to last and keep its shape.
notes.2: Melamine is used to make the container, not to be eaten. Melamine in food is harmful. Think about the properties a container needs.

why.right: Melamine suits containers because its properties match what a container must do, such as holding food without breaking.
wrong: Melamine suits containers because heat passes through it quickly, which keeps the food inside warm for longer.
Melamine suits containers because it is a natural substance that is safe to eat in any amount.

questions.q: Babies became ill from milk powder mixed with melamine. This shows melamine is
questions.explain: The babies became ill after drinking milk powder with melamine in it. This shows that melamine is harmful when it is added to food.
questions.lo: State why knowing the chemical composition of everyday items matters (useful or harmful, recycling)

notes.1: The babies became ill, so the melamine did not help them. Think about what an illness after eating a substance shows about that substance.
notes.2: Melamine was added to make the milk powder seem richer in protein, but it is not a real source of protein. The babies became ill after drinking it.
notes.3: Melamine is made of more than one element chemically combined. Also, the question is about what the babies' illness shows about melamine in food.

why.right: Melamine is harmful in food because babies who drank milk powder containing it became ill.
wrong: Melamine is harmful in food because every substance made in a factory is poisonous to people.
Melamine is harmful in food because any substance made of more than one element is poisonous.

questions.q: Why do we need to know what waste materials are made of?
choices: to find out how heavy they are
to make them break down faster
questions.explain: Different materials must be recycled in different ways. Knowing what waste is made of lets it be sorted and recycled correctly.
questions.lo: State why knowing the chemical composition of everyday items matters (useful or harmful, recycling)

notes.0: The mass of waste can be found by weighing it, without knowing what it is made of. Think about what happens to waste after it is collected and sorted.
notes.2: Knowing what waste is made of does not make it break down any faster. Think about how different materials are sorted so they can be used again.
notes.3: Knowing what waste is made of does not change how harmful it is. Think about how different materials are sorted so they can be used again.

why.right: Knowing what waste is made of matters because each material must be sorted and recycled by a suitable method.
wrong: Knowing what waste is made of matters because all waste materials can be melted together into one new material.
Knowing what waste is made of matters because every kind of waste can be burnt safely once it is identified.

questions.q: Elements are
choices: two or more substances chemically combined
the basic building blocks of matter
substances made in a chemical reaction
questions.explain: Elements are the basic building blocks of matter. All other substances are made from elements.
questions.lo: State that elements are the basic building blocks of matter and cannot be broken down

notes.0: A mixture of compounds contains many substances, so it is not basic. Elements are the simplest substances, and compounds are made from them.
notes.1: Two or more substances chemically combined describes a compound, not an element. Think about the simplest substances that everything else is made from.
notes.3: This describes how compounds are formed. Elements are the simplest substances, and other substances are built up from them.

questions.q: Which statement about elements is correct?
choices: they cannot be broken down into simpler substances
they are formed by a chemical reaction
they contain two or more substances
questions.explain: An element cannot be broken down into simpler substances. This is why elements are the basic building blocks of matter.
questions.lo: State that elements are the basic building blocks of matter and cannot be broken down

notes.0: Easy separation is a property of mixtures. An element is a single pure substance, so there is nothing in it to separate out.
notes.2: Formed by a chemical reaction describes a compound. Think about what happens when someone tries to break an element down into anything simpler.
notes.3: Containing two or more substances describes a compound or a mixture. An element is only one substance. Think about whether it can be made any simpler.

why.right: An element cannot be broken down because it is made up of only one type of atom.
wrong: An element cannot be broken down because its particles are packed too tightly to be pulled apart.
An element cannot be broken down because it is always a hard solid at room temperature.

questions.q: Elements are grouped by their properties in the
questions.explain: The Periodic Table of Elements lists all the known elements. Elements with similar properties are placed in the same group.
questions.lo: State that elements are the basic building blocks of matter and cannot be broken down

notes.1: Mixtures are not elements, so a list of mixtures would not group elements. Think about the chart that shows every known element with its symbol.
notes.2: Compounds are made of elements, but a table of compounds does not arrange the elements themselves. Think about the chart where every element has a box and symbol.
notes.3: A density table lists how dense materials are. It does not group elements by their properties. Think about the chart that lists every known element.

questions.q: Is copper (Cu) a metal or a non-metal?
questions.explain: Copper is on the left of the zigzag line in the Periodic Table, where the metals are. It is shiny and conducts heat and electricity well.
questions.lo: Classify elements as metals or non-metals using the Periodic Table

notes.0: Copper has one symbol, Cu, in the Periodic Table, so it is an element. A compound has two or more elements chemically combined.
notes.1: Copper is shiny and is used in electrical wires because it conducts electricity well. Compare these properties and its place in the Periodic Table with the zigzag line.

why.right: Copper is a metal because it lies to the left of the zigzag line in the Periodic Table.
wrong: Copper is a metal because it is a solid, and every solid element is a metal.
Copper is a metal because it has a symbol made of two letters in the Periodic Table.

questions.q: Is sulfur (S) a metal or a non-metal?
questions.explain: Sulfur is on the right of the zigzag line in the Periodic Table, where the non-metals are. It is a dull yellow solid that does not conduct electricity.
questions.lo: Classify elements as metals or non-metals using the Periodic Table

notes.1: Being a solid does not make an element a metal. Sulfur is dull and brittle and does not conduct electricity. Check where it sits in the Periodic Table.
notes.2: Sulfur has one symbol, S, in the Periodic Table, so it is an element. A compound has two or more elements chemically combined.

why.right: Sulfur is a non-metal because it lies to the right of the zigzag line in the Periodic Table.
wrong: Sulfur is a non-metal because it is yellow, and every coloured element is a non-metal.
Sulfur is a non-metal because it has a symbol made of only one letter.

questions.q: Is nitrogen (N) a metal or a non-metal?
questions.explain: Nitrogen is on the right of the zigzag line in the Periodic Table, where the non-metals are. It is a gas at room temperature and does not conduct electricity.
questions.lo: Classify elements as metals or non-metals using the Periodic Table

notes.0: Metals are usually shiny solids that conduct electricity. Nitrogen is a colourless gas that does not conduct electricity. Check where it sits in the Periodic Table.
notes.2: Nitrogen has one symbol, N, in the Periodic Table, so it is an element. A compound has two or more elements chemically combined.

why.right: Nitrogen is a non-metal because it lies to the right of the zigzag line in the Periodic Table.
wrong: Nitrogen is a non-metal because it is a gas, and only gases can be non-metals.
Nitrogen is a non-metal because it has a symbol made of only one letter.

questions.q: Which element is a non-metal?
questions.explain: Oxygen is on the right of the zigzag line in the Periodic Table, so it is a non-metal. Aluminium, iron and sodium are all metals.
questions.lo: Classify elements as metals or non-metals using the Periodic Table

notes.0: Aluminium is shiny and conducts electricity well, so it is used in drink cans and cables. Look for the element that lies to the right of the zigzag line.
notes.1: Iron is a strong, shiny solid that conducts electricity. These are properties of metals. Look for the element that lies to the right of the zigzag line.
notes.2: Sodium is soft, but it is shiny when freshly cut and conducts electricity. Look for the element that lies to the right of the zigzag line.

why.right: Oxygen is a non-metal because it lies to the right of the zigzag line in the Periodic Table.
wrong: Oxygen is a non-metal because it is needed for burning, and metals can never burn.
Oxygen is a non-metal because it is invisible, and only invisible elements are non-metals.

questions.q: Which element is a metal?
questions.explain: Zinc is on the left of the zigzag line in the Periodic Table, so it is a metal. Chlorine, neon and carbon are non-metals.
questions.lo: Classify elements as metals or non-metals using the Periodic Table

notes.0: Chlorine is a yellowish-green gas that does not conduct electricity, so it is a non-metal. Look for the element that lies to the left of the zigzag line.
notes.1: Neon is a colourless gas at room temperature, which is a property of a non-metal. Look for the element that lies to the left of the zigzag line.
notes.2: Carbon is a solid, but being a solid does not make an element a metal. Carbon lies to the right of the zigzag line in the Periodic Table.

why.right: Zinc is a metal because it lies to the left of the zigzag line in the Periodic Table.
wrong: Zinc is a metal because it is a solid, and every solid element is a metal.
Zinc is a metal because it has a symbol made of two letters in the Periodic Table.

questions.q: Compounds consist of two or more elements that are
questions.explain: A compound is made of two or more elements that are chemically combined. The elements are joined in a chemical reaction and are hard to separate.
questions.lo: Identify the elements that make up a compound

notes.0: Elements that are not chemically combined form a mixture. Think about how the elements in a compound are joined in a chemical reaction.
notes.1: Physically mixed elements form a mixture, and they can be separated easily. Think about how the elements in a compound are joined.
notes.3: Compounds can be solid, liquid or gas. Water is a liquid and salt is a solid. Think about how the elements in a compound are joined.

questions.q: Which elements make up water?
questions.explain: Water is a compound of hydrogen and oxygen chemically combined. Each water molecule has two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
questions.lo: Identify the elements that make up a compound

notes.1: Carbon and oxygen make up carbon dioxide, not water. Water contains no carbon. Think about the two gases that react together to form water.
notes.2: Hydrogen and nitrogen make up ammonia. Water contains no nitrogen. Think about the two gases that react together to form water.
notes.3: Sodium is a metal, and pure water contains no sodium. Think about the two gases that react together to form water.

questions.q: Which elements make up sodium chloride?
questions.explain: The name sodium chloride shows the elements it contains. Sodium chloride is made of sodium and chlorine chemically combined.
questions.lo: Identify the elements that make up a compound

notes.0: Sodium chloride contains no hydrogen. The name of a compound shows the elements in it. Look at both parts of the name.
notes.1: The ending chloride stands for chlorine, not oxygen. Look at both parts of the name sodium chloride.
notes.3: Carbon and oxygen together would give the ending carbonate. Look at the ending of the name sodium chloride.

why.right: Sodium chloride contains sodium and chlorine because the ending chloride in a name stands for chlorine.
wrong: Sodium chloride contains sodium and chlorine because all salts are made of these two elements.
Sodium chloride contains sodium and chlorine because the two elements are mixed but not combined.

questions.q: Which elements make up carbon dioxide?
questions.explain: The name carbon dioxide shows that it contains carbon and oxygen. Each molecule has one carbon atom and two oxygen atoms.
questions.lo: Identify the elements that make up a compound

notes.0: Carbon only would be the element carbon, not a compound. The word dioxide in the name stands for another element. Think about what oxide means.
notes.1: Carbon dioxide contains no nitrogen. The word carbon is in the name. Think about which element the word dioxide stands for.
notes.2: Carbon and hydrogen form compounds found in fuels. The word dioxide in the name does not stand for hydrogen. Think about what oxide means.

why.right: Carbon dioxide contains carbon and oxygen because the word oxide in a name stands for oxygen.
wrong: Carbon dioxide contains carbon and oxygen because it is a mixture of carbon powder and air.
Carbon dioxide contains carbon and oxygen because every gas in the air contains some oxygen atoms.

questions.q: Which elements make up ammonia?
questions.explain: Ammonia is a compound of nitrogen and hydrogen chemically combined. Each ammonia molecule has one nitrogen atom and three hydrogen atoms.
questions.lo: Identify the elements that make up a compound

notes.0: Ammonia contains no carbon. It is made of two gases chemically combined. One of them makes up most of the air.
notes.2: Nitrogen and oxygen are the two main gases in air, and air is a mixture. Ammonia contains no oxygen. Think about the other element it contains.
notes.3: Hydrogen and oxygen make up water. Ammonia contains no oxygen. Think about which gas, found mostly in air, is in ammonia.

questions.q: Calcium carbonate contains which elements?
questions.explain: The name calcium carbonate shows calcium, and the ending carbonate stands for carbon and oxygen. So calcium carbonate contains three elements.
questions.lo: Identify the elements that make up a compound

notes.0: The ending carbonate stands for more than carbon. Compare it with carbon dioxide and think about which other element it includes.
notes.2: The first word, calcium, is an element too. Calcium carbonate is named after all of the elements it contains.
notes.3: The ending carbonate stands for carbon, not chlorine. Chlorine would give the ending chloride. Look again at the ending of the name.

why.right: Calcium carbonate contains three elements because the ending carbonate stands for both carbon and oxygen.
wrong: Calcium carbonate contains three elements because every compound is made of exactly three elements.
Calcium carbonate contains three elements because it is a mixture of chalk, carbon and air.

questions.q: A compound contains only hydrogen and oxygen. Which could it be?
questions.explain: Water is made of hydrogen and oxygen only. The other compounds contain carbon, nitrogen, sodium or chlorine.
questions.lo: Identify the elements that make up a compound

notes.0: Carbon dioxide contains oxygen, but it also contains carbon and no hydrogen. Look for the compound made only of hydrogen and oxygen.
notes.1: Ammonia contains hydrogen, but it also contains nitrogen and no oxygen. Look for the compound made only of hydrogen and oxygen.
notes.3: Sodium chloride contains sodium and chlorine, with no hydrogen or oxygen. Look for the compound made only of hydrogen and oxygen.

questions.q: Which statement about compounds is correct?
choices: they have different properties from their elements
they keep the properties of their elements
their elements are in any proportion
questions.explain: When elements combine to form a compound, a new substance is made. The compound has its own properties, which are different from those of its elements.
questions.lo: Compare the properties of a compound with its constituent elements

notes.1: Keeping the properties of the constituents describes a mixture. In a compound, the elements have reacted to form a new substance.
notes.2: Elements that separate easily are found in a mixture. The elements in a compound are chemically combined and need a chemical reaction to separate.
notes.3: Constituents in any proportion describes a mixture. In a compound, the elements are combined in a set ratio.

why.right: A compound has new properties because its elements have reacted to form a completely new substance.
wrong: A compound has new properties because its elements are only mixed and lose their colour.
A compound has new properties because heating the elements always makes them change state.

questions.q: The elements in a compound are combined in
choices: a proportion that changes with time
questions.explain: The elements in a compound are always combined in a fixed proportion by mass. For example, water always has the same ratio of hydrogen to oxygen.
questions.lo: Compare the properties of a compound with its constituent elements

notes.0: Any proportion describes a mixture, such as a sugar solution that can be made weak or strong. A compound always has the same make-up.
notes.1: Equal volumes is not a rule for compounds, and many compounds contain more of one element than another. Think about the mass of each element.
notes.2: A compound does not change its make-up over time. Water made today has the same make-up as water made long ago.

why.right: The proportion in a compound is fixed because the elements always combine in the same ratio when it forms.
wrong: The proportion in a compound is fixed because a compound always contains equal masses of each element.
The proportion in a compound is fixed because the elements are measured out by hand before mixing.

questions.q: hydrogen (gas) + oxygen (gas) --> water. What is the state of water at room temperature?
questions.explain: Water is a liquid at room temperature, even though hydrogen and oxygen are gases. A compound has different properties from its elements.
questions.lo: Compare the properties of a compound with its constituent elements

notes.0: Water is a solid only below 0 °C, which is ice. Room temperature is about 25 °C. Think about the water that comes out of a tap.
notes.1: Hydrogen and oxygen are gases, but a compound does not keep the properties of its elements. Think about how water looks in a glass at room temperature.

why.right: Water is a liquid because a compound has its own properties, which differ from those of its elements.
wrong: Water is a liquid because two gases always form a liquid when they are mixed.
Water is a liquid because hydrogen and oxygen turn into liquids whenever they cool to room temperature.

questions.q: carbon (solid) + oxygen (gas) --> carbon dioxide. What is the state of carbon dioxide?
questions.explain: Carbon dioxide is a gas, even though carbon is a solid. A compound has different properties from its elements.
questions.lo: Compare the properties of a compound with its constituent elements

notes.0: Carbon is a solid, but a compound does not keep the properties of its elements. Think about the gas that people breathe out.
notes.2: Carbon dioxide is not a liquid at room temperature. Think about the gas that people breathe out and that makes the bubbles in soft drinks.

why.right: Carbon dioxide is a gas because a compound has its own properties, which differ from those of its elements.
wrong: Carbon dioxide is a gas because the carbon in it is burnt away, leaving only oxygen gas.
Carbon dioxide is a gas because a solid always turns into a gas when it is heated in air.

questions.q: Why is it hard to obtain hydrogen and oxygen from water?
choices: breaking it down needs a lot of energy
questions.explain: Water is a compound, so hydrogen and oxygen are chemically combined in it. Breaking water down needs a chemical reaction that uses a lot of energy, such as passing electricity through it.
questions.lo: Compare the properties of a compound with its constituent elements

notes.0: If water were a mixture, its constituents could be separated easily. Water is a compound, so its elements are chemically combined.
notes.1: Water does have constituent elements, which are hydrogen and oxygen. Think about how strongly they are held together in the compound.
notes.2: Water is not an element, because it can be broken down into hydrogen and oxygen. Think about what that breaking down needs.

why.right: Water is hard to break down because its hydrogen and oxygen are chemically combined, not just mixed.
wrong: Water is hard to break down because hydrogen and oxygen cannot be separated by any method.
Water is hard to break down because it is a mixture of two gases that dissolve in each other.

questions.q: Sodium chloride is safe to eat but chlorine is harmful. This shows a compound
choices: has different properties from its elements
is a mixture of its elements
has the same properties as its elements
questions.explain: Chlorine is a poisonous gas, but sodium chloride is safe to eat in small amounts. This shows that a compound has different properties from its elements.
questions.lo: Compare the properties of a compound with its constituent elements

notes.1: The question compares how safe chlorine and sodium chloride are. It is not about separating them. Think about whether the compound behaves like its elements.
notes.2: In a mixture, chlorine would keep its harmful property. Sodium chloride is safe to eat, so the chlorine in it is chemically combined.
notes.3: If the compound had the same properties as chlorine, it would be harmful to eat. Compare how chlorine and sodium chloride affect the body.

why.right: Sodium chloride is safe because a compound has new properties that differ from those of its elements.
wrong: Sodium chloride is safe because the harmful chlorine has been removed from it during cooking.
Sodium chloride is safe because sodium cancels out the harm of chlorine in a mixture.

questions.q: A mixture is made up of two or more substances that are
questions.explain: A mixture is made of two or more substances that are not chemically combined. Each substance keeps its own properties.
questions.lo: Describe a mixture and state that it keeps the properties of its constituents

notes.0: A fixed proportion describes a compound. The substances in a mixture can be present in any amounts.
notes.1: Mixtures can contain elements, compounds or both. Salt solution is a mixture of two compounds. Think about how the substances in a mixture are held together.
notes.3: Chemically combined describes a compound. Think about whether the substances in a mixture react with each other.

questions.q: Which statement about mixtures is correct?
choices: they keep the properties of their constituents
their constituents are in a fixed proportion
their constituents are hard to separate
questions.explain: The substances in a mixture are not chemically combined. So each substance keeps its own properties, and no new substance is formed.
questions.lo: Describe a mixture and state that it keeps the properties of its constituents

notes.0: New properties appear when a new substance is formed in a chemical reaction. That happens when a compound forms, not when substances are mixed.
notes.2: A fixed proportion describes a compound. A mixture such as sugar solution can have any amount of sugar.
notes.3: Constituents that are hard to separate describe a compound. The parts of a mixture can be separated by physical methods such as filtering.

why.right: A mixture keeps the properties of its constituents because they are not chemically combined.
wrong: A mixture keeps the properties of its constituents because they are in a fixed proportion.
A mixture keeps the properties of its constituents because they react to form a new substance.

questions.q: Salt solution tastes salty because a mixture
choices: keeps the properties of its constituents
has a fixed proportion of constituents
is formed by a chemical reaction
questions.explain: Salt solution is a mixture of salt and water. The salt keeps its salty taste because it is not chemically combined with the water.
questions.lo: Describe a mixture and state that it keeps the properties of its constituents

notes.1: If the mixture had new properties, the salty taste would be lost. The salty taste comes from the salt itself.
notes.2: Salt solution can be made with any amount of salt, so its proportion is not fixed. Think about where the salty taste comes from.
notes.3: Dissolving salt is a physical change, not a chemical reaction. No new substance is formed. Think about where the salty taste comes from.

why.right: Salt solution tastes salty because the dissolved salt is not chemically combined with the water.
wrong: Salt solution tastes salty because salt and water react to form a new salty substance.
Salt solution tastes salty because water itself has a salty taste once it is heated.

questions.q: Which gas makes up about 78% of air?
questions.explain: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of air. Oxygen makes up about 21%, and the rest includes argon, carbon dioxide and water vapour.
questions.lo: Describe air as a mixture whose constituents vary in amount

notes.0: Oxygen makes up only about 21% of air, even though it is the gas needed for breathing. Think about the gas found in the largest amount.
notes.1: Water vapour is present in small, changing amounts. Think about the gas found in the largest amount in air.
notes.2: Carbon dioxide makes up only about 0.04% of air. Think about the gas found in the largest amount.

questions.q: Which constituent of air varies most with time and place?
questions.explain: The amount of carbon dioxide changes from place to place and over time. It is higher near traffic and factories, where fuels are burnt.
questions.lo: Describe air as a mixture whose constituents vary in amount

notes.0: Nitrogen stays at about 78% of air almost everywhere. Think about which gas is added to the air by traffic and factories.
notes.2: Oxygen stays at about 21% of air almost everywhere. Think about which gas is added to the air by traffic and factories.

why.right: Carbon dioxide varies the most because burning fuels add it and plants remove it, by different amounts in different places.
wrong: Carbon dioxide varies the most because it is the gas found in the largest amount in air.
Carbon dioxide varies the most because it is a pure element that reacts with every other gas.

questions.q: Steel is a mixture of iron, carbon and other elements. It is made up of
questions.explain: Iron and carbon are elements. Steel is a mixture of iron, carbon and other elements, so it is made up of elements only.
questions.lo: Classify mixtures as made of elements only, compounds only, or both

notes.0: Iron and carbon each have one symbol in the Periodic Table. Check whether each constituent of steel is an element or a compound.
notes.1: Look at each constituent named. Iron and carbon each appear as one symbol in the Periodic Table. Decide whether any constituent is a compound.

why.right: Steel is made of elements only because iron, carbon and its other constituents are all single elements.
wrong: Steel is made of elements only because any mixture containing a metal is made of elements only.
Steel is made of elements only because its constituents have reacted to form one new element.

questions.q: Salt solution is a mixture of sodium chloride and water. It is made up of
questions.explain: Sodium chloride and water are both compounds. So salt solution is a mixture made up of compounds only.
questions.lo: Classify mixtures as made of elements only, compounds only, or both

notes.1: Sodium and chlorine are elements, but in salt they are chemically combined. Decide whether each constituent of salt solution is an element or a compound.
notes.2: Sodium chloride and water each contain more than one element chemically combined. Decide whether that makes each of them an element or a compound.

why.right: Salt solution is made of compounds only because sodium chloride and water each contain chemically combined elements.
wrong: Salt solution is made of compounds only because dissolving salt in water forms a new compound.
Salt solution is made of compounds only because every liquid mixture is made of compounds only.

questions.q: Seawater contains sodium chloride, water and a little iodine. It is made up of
questions.explain: Sodium chloride and water are compounds, and iodine is an element. So seawater is made up of both elements and compounds.
questions.lo: Classify mixtures as made of elements only, compounds only, or both

notes.0: Sodium chloride and water each contain more than one element chemically combined, so they are not elements. Check every constituent before deciding.
notes.1: Iodine has one symbol, I, in the Periodic Table, so it is not a compound. Check every constituent before deciding.

why.right: Seawater contains elements and compounds because water is a compound and iodine is an element.
wrong: Seawater contains elements and compounds because salt breaks up into sodium and chlorine elements in water.
Seawater contains elements and compounds because every mixture found in nature contains both elements and compounds.

questions.q: Pewter is a mixture of tin, copper and silver. It is made up of
questions.explain: Tin, copper and silver are all elements. So pewter is a mixture made up of elements only.
questions.lo: Classify mixtures as made of elements only, compounds only, or both

notes.1: Tin, copper and silver each have one symbol in the Periodic Table. Check whether any constituent of pewter is a compound.
notes.2: Tin, copper and silver are each a single substance with one symbol in the Periodic Table. Decide whether they are elements or compounds.

why.right: Pewter is made of elements only because tin, copper and silver are each single elements.
wrong: Pewter is made of elements only because the metals react to form one new element.
Pewter is made of elements only because any hard solid mixture contains no compounds.

questions.q: Concrete contains calcium carbonate, silicon dioxide and water. It is made up of
questions.explain: Calcium carbonate, silicon dioxide and water each contain elements chemically combined. So concrete is made up of compounds only.
questions.lo: Classify mixtures as made of elements only, compounds only, or both

notes.0: Each constituent named has more than one element in it. For example, water contains hydrogen and oxygen. Decide whether that makes them elements or compounds.
notes.2: Silicon dioxide contains silicon and oxygen chemically combined, so it is not an element. Check each constituent of concrete in the same way.

why.right: Concrete is made of compounds only because each of its constituents contains chemically combined elements.
wrong: Concrete is made of compounds only because every hard building material is a compound.
Concrete is made of compounds only because water turns every substance it touches into a compound.

questions.q: A mixture is made up of elements only. Which could it be?
choices: a mixture of sugar and water
a mixture of salt and water
a mixture of sand and water
a mixture of nitrogen and oxygen
questions.explain: Nitrogen and oxygen are both elements. Sugar, salt, sand and water are compounds, so the other mixtures contain compounds.
questions.lo: Classify mixtures as made of elements only, compounds only, or both

notes.0: Sugar and water each contain more than one element chemically combined. Look for a mixture in which every constituent is an element.
notes.1: Salt and water are both compounds. Look for a mixture in which every constituent is an element.
notes.2: Sand is mostly silicon dioxide and water contains hydrogen and oxygen, so both are compounds. Look for a mixture in which every constituent is an element.

why.right: A nitrogen and oxygen mixture contains elements only because each of the two gases is an element.
wrong: A nitrogen and oxygen mixture contains elements only because every gas is an element.
A nitrogen and oxygen mixture contains elements only because the two gases react to form a new element.

questions.q: In a solution, the substance that dissolves is the
questions.explain: The solute is the substance that dissolves. The solvent is the substance it dissolves in, and together they form a solution.
questions.lo: Identify the solute, solvent and solution

notes.0: The solvent is the substance that does the dissolving, such as water. Think about the name for the substance that disappears into it.
notes.1: A suspension contains insoluble substances that do not dissolve. Think about the name for the substance that does dissolve.
notes.2: A mixture is the general name for substances mixed together. Think about the name for the substance that dissolves in a solution.

questions.q: In a solution, the substance in which the solute dissolves is the
questions.explain: The solvent is the substance in which the solute dissolves. Water is the most common solvent.
questions.lo: Identify the solute, solvent and solution

notes.0: A suspension contains solids that do not dissolve. Think about the substance that does the dissolving, such as water.
notes.2: The solute is the substance that dissolves. Think about the name for the substance that it dissolves in.
notes.3: A compound is two or more elements chemically combined. Think about the name for the substance that a solute dissolves in.

questions.q: Sugar dissolves in water to form sugar solution. Which is the solute?
questions.explain: The solute is the substance that dissolves. Sugar dissolves in water, so sugar is the solute.
questions.lo: Identify the solute, solvent and solution

notes.0: Sugar solution is the mixture formed at the end, which is the solution. Think about which substance dissolves.
notes.1: Water is the substance that the sugar dissolves in, so it is the solvent. Think about which substance dissolves.

why.right: Sugar is the solute because it is the substance that dissolves in the water.
wrong: Sugar is the solute because it is the substance present in the larger amount.
Sugar is the solute because it is the liquid that the other substance dissolves in.

questions.q: Salt dissolves in water to form salt solution. Which is the solvent?
questions.explain: The solvent is the substance in which the solute dissolves. Salt dissolves in water, so water is the solvent.
questions.lo: Identify the solute, solvent and solution

notes.1: Salt is the substance that dissolves, so it is the solute. Think about the substance it dissolves in.
notes.2: Salt solution is the mixture formed at the end. Think about the substance the salt dissolves in.

why.right: Water is the solvent because it is the substance in which the salt dissolves.
wrong: Water is the solvent because it is the substance that dissolves into the salt.
Water is the solvent because it is the substance present in the smaller amount.

questions.q: Iodine dissolves in alcohol. Which is the solute?
questions.explain: Iodine is the substance that dissolves, so it is the solute. Alcohol is the solvent, and the mixture is iodine solution.
questions.lo: Identify the solute, solvent and solution

notes.1: Alcohol is the liquid that the iodine dissolves in, so it is the solvent. Think about which substance dissolves.
notes.2: Iodine solution is the mixture formed at the end. Think about which substance dissolves to make it.

why.right: Iodine is the solute because it is the substance that dissolves in the alcohol.
wrong: Iodine is the solute because it is the substance that the alcohol dissolves into.
Iodine is the solute because it is the substance present in the larger amount.

questions.q: Cup A has more sugar dissolved in the same volume of water. Cup A is
questions.explain: A concentrated solution has more solute dissolved in a given volume of solvent. Cup A has more sugar in the same volume of water, so it is more concentrated.
questions.lo: Identify the solute, solvent and solution

notes.0: The sugar has dissolved, so Cup A is a solution, not a suspension. Think about how much solute is in the same volume of water.
notes.1: Cup A contains sugar and water, so it is a mixture, not a pure substance. Think about how much solute is in the same volume of water.
notes.2: A dilute solution has less solute in a given volume of solvent. Compare the amount of sugar in Cup A with the other cup.

why.right: A solution is more concentrated when it has more solute dissolved in the same volume of solvent.
wrong: A solution is more concentrated when it has more solvent for the same amount of solute.
A solution is more concentrated when its solute has dissolved more quickly than in another solution.

questions.q: The rate of dissolving refers to
choices: how quickly a solute dissolves in a solvent
questions.explain: The rate of dissolving is how quickly a solute dissolves in a solvent. It is different from solubility, which is how well a solute dissolves.
questions.lo: Predict how a factor changes the rate of dissolving

notes.0: How well a solute dissolves describes solubility. The word rate is about time, so think about speed.
notes.1: The colour of a solution does not describe dissolving. The word rate is about time, so think about speed.
notes.3: The amount of solvent used is not a rate. The word rate is about time, so think about speed.

questions.q: Which sugar dissolves fastest in water?
questions.explain: Fine sugar has the smallest pieces, so more of its surface is in contact with the water. This makes it dissolve fastest.
questions.lo: Predict how a factor changes the rate of dissolving

notes.0: Rock sugar is in large lumps, so less of its surface touches the water. Think about which form has the smallest pieces.
notes.2: Sugar cubes are large blocks, so the water reaches only their outer surface at first. Think about which form has the smallest pieces.

why.right: Fine sugar dissolves fastest because its small pieces have a larger total surface area in contact with water.
wrong: Fine sugar dissolves fastest because its small pieces have a higher solubility than large lumps.
Fine sugar dissolves fastest because its small pieces are lighter and so they float on the water.

questions.q: In which water does sugar dissolve fastest?
questions.explain: Sugar dissolves faster at higher temperatures. Hot water at 80 °C is the hottest, so sugar dissolves fastest in it.
questions.lo: Predict how a factor changes the rate of dissolving

notes.0: Water at 20 °C is not the warmest choice. Think about how raising the temperature of water changes the rate of dissolving.
notes.1: Cold water slows dissolving down. Think about how raising the temperature of water changes the rate of dissolving.
notes.2: Water at 30 °C is warm, but it is not the warmest choice. Think about how raising the temperature changes the rate of dissolving.

why.right: Sugar dissolves faster in hot water because the particles move faster and mix more quickly.
wrong: Sugar dissolves faster in hot water because heat makes the sugar pieces melt into liquid sugar.
Sugar dissolves faster in hot water because heating makes the water particles bigger, leaving more space.

questions.q: Coffee powder is stirred faster. The rate of dissolving will
questions.explain: Stirring brings fresh solvent into contact with the coffee powder. So stirring faster increases the rate of dissolving.
questions.lo: Predict how a factor changes the rate of dissolving

notes.0: Stirring helps the solute and solvent mix, so it does not slow dissolving. Think about what moving the liquid around does to the powder.
notes.2: Stirring does change how quickly a solute dissolves. Think about what moving the liquid around does to the powder.

why.right: Faster stirring speeds up dissolving because it keeps bringing fresh solvent into contact with the solute.
wrong: Faster stirring speeds up dissolving because it makes more solute able to dissolve in the solvent.
Faster stirring speeds up dissolving because it heats the water up to its boiling point.

questions.q: A sugar cube dissolved slowly. Which change makes it dissolve faster?
questions.explain: Crushing the cube breaks it into small pieces with a larger total surface area. More of the sugar touches the water, so it dissolves faster.
questions.lo: Predict how a factor changes the rate of dissolving

notes.0: Stirring more slowly mixes the sugar and water less, so dissolving slows down. Think about how to get more sugar touching the water.
notes.1: A bigger cube has less surface area for its size, so it dissolves more slowly. Think about how to get more sugar touching the water.
notes.3: Colder water slows dissolving down. Think about how to get more of the sugar touching the water.

why.right: Crushing a sugar cube speeds up dissolving because the small pieces have a larger total surface area.
wrong: Crushing a sugar cube speeds up dissolving because it changes the sugar into a new substance.
Crushing a sugar cube speeds up dissolving because it raises the solubility of the sugar.

questions.q: How well a solute dissolves in a fixed volume of a particular solvent is its
questions.explain: Solubility is how well a solute dissolves in a fixed volume of a particular solvent. It is not about how fast the solute dissolves.
questions.lo: Distinguish rate of dissolving from solubility and state factors affecting solubility

notes.1: Rate of dissolving is about how quickly a solute dissolves. This question is about how well it dissolves in a fixed volume.
notes.2: Density is the mass per unit volume of a material and does not describe dissolving. Think about the term for how well a solute dissolves.
notes.3: Concentration describes how much solute is already in a solution. Think about the term for how well a solute can dissolve in a solvent.

questions.q: Which is a factor that affects solubility?
questions.explain: Solubility depends on the type of solute, the type of solvent and the temperature. Stirring and particle size only change how fast the solute dissolves.
questions.lo: Distinguish rate of dissolving from solubility and state factors affecting solubility

notes.0: The shape of the beaker does not change how much solute dissolves. Think about factors that change how much solute can dissolve.
notes.1: Stirring changes how fast a solute dissolves, not how much can dissolve. Think about factors that change how much solute can dissolve.
notes.2: Particle size changes how fast a solute dissolves, not how much can dissolve. Think about factors that change how much solute can dissolve.

why.right: The type of solvent affects solubility because a solute can dissolve well in one solvent but not in another.
wrong: The type of solvent affects solubility because some solvents make the solute dissolve faster when stirred.
The type of solvent affects solubility because a solvent changes the size of the solute particles.

questions.q: Salt dissolves in water but not in oil. This shows solubility depends on
questions.explain: Salt is the same solute in both cases, but water and oil are different solvents. So the solubility of salt depends on the type of solvent.
questions.lo: Distinguish rate of dissolving from solubility and state factors affecting solubility

notes.0: No stirring is compared in this test. Think about what is different between the two cases.
notes.2: The same salt is used in both cases, so the particle size is not what changes. Think about what is different between the two cases.
notes.3: The solute is salt in both cases, so it does not change. Think about what is different between the two cases.

why.right: Salt dissolves in water but not in oil because the same solute can dissolve in one solvent but not another.
wrong: Salt dissolves in water but not in oil because oil is stirred more slowly than water.
Salt dissolves in water but not in oil because oil makes the salt particles too large.

questions.q: In the same volume of water, more sugar dissolves than flour. This shows solubility depends on
questions.explain: Water is the solvent in both cases, but sugar and flour are different solutes. So solubility depends on the type of solute.
questions.lo: Distinguish rate of dissolving from solubility and state factors affecting solubility

notes.0: Water is the solvent in both cases, so the solvent does not change. Think about what is different between the two cases.
notes.1: The room temperature is not what is being changed here. Think about what is different between the two cases.
notes.3: Stirring changes how fast a solute dissolves, not how much dissolves. Think about what is different between the two cases.

why.right: More sugar than flour dissolves in water because different solutes have different solubilities in the same solvent.
wrong: More sugar than flour dissolves in water because sugar is stirred faster than flour.
More sugar than flour dissolves in water because sugar reacts with water to form a new compound.

questions.q: A substance does not dissolve in a solvent. It is described as
questions.explain: A substance that does not dissolve in a solvent is insoluble. Sand is insoluble in water.
questions.lo: Distinguish rate of dissolving from solubility and state factors affecting solubility

notes.0: Soluble means a substance can dissolve. This substance does not dissolve. Think about the term for a substance that cannot dissolve.
notes.1: Concentrated describes a solution with a lot of solute dissolved in it. Here nothing has dissolved. Think about the term for a substance that does not dissolve.
notes.2: Dilute describes a solution with little solute dissolved in it. Here nothing has dissolved. Think about the term for a substance that does not dissolve.

questions.q: A suspension is a mixture that contains
questions.explain: A suspension contains insoluble solid particles spread through a liquid. The particles do not dissolve and settle over time.
questions.lo: Classify mixtures as solutions or suspensions from observations

notes.1: One element alone is not a mixture, and a suspension is a mixture. Think about substances that do not dissolve.
notes.2: A solute that dissolves completely forms a solution. Think about what happens to substances that do not dissolve.
notes.3: Elements chemically combined form a compound, and a suspension is a mixture. Think about substances that do not dissolve.

questions.q: Light passes fully through a liquid and nothing settles. What is it?
questions.explain: In a solution the solute has dissolved completely. The liquid is clear, light passes through it, and nothing settles at the bottom.
questions.lo: Classify mixtures as solutions or suspensions from observations

notes.0: This liquid is described by how light passes through it and whether anything settles. These are tests used to sort mixtures, not elements.
notes.2: A suspension is cloudy, blocks some light and has solids settling at the bottom. Compare this with the liquid described.

why.right: A solution lets light through because its solute particles are dissolved and too small to block light.
wrong: A solution lets light through because its solid particles are large and sink to the bottom quickly.
A solution lets light through because it contains only the pure solvent and no other substance.

questions.q: A liquid is cloudy and solid deposits form at the bottom. What is it?
questions.explain: A suspension is cloudy because it contains insoluble particles. Over time the particles settle as solid deposits at the bottom.
questions.lo: Classify mixtures as solutions or suspensions from observations

notes.1: A solution is clear and nothing settles out of it. Think about mixtures with particles that do not dissolve.
notes.2: A compound is a single substance with elements chemically combined. Solids settling out shows that more than one substance is present.

why.right: A suspension is cloudy because its insoluble particles are large enough to block light and settle.
wrong: A suspension is cloudy because its particles have dissolved completely in the solvent.
A suspension is cloudy because its elements are chemically combined into a new substance.

questions.q: Is soda water a solution or a suspension?
questions.explain: Soda water is carbon dioxide dissolved in water. It is clear, and no solid settles at the bottom, so it is a solution.
questions.lo: Classify mixtures as solutions or suspensions from observations

notes.0: Soda water contains carbon dioxide and water mixed, not chemically combined into one substance. Think about whether it is clear or cloudy.
notes.1: A suspension is cloudy and has solids that settle. Soda water is clear. Think about what happens to the carbon dioxide in it.

why.right: Soda water is a solution because the carbon dioxide is dissolved completely and nothing settles out.
wrong: Soda water is a solution because the gas bubbles are solid particles that sink to the bottom.
Soda water is a solution because it is cloudy and blocks light from passing through.

questions.q: Is calamine lotion a solution or a suspension?
questions.explain: Calamine lotion is cloudy, and its solid particles settle at the bottom. The bottle must be shaken before use, so it is a suspension.
questions.lo: Classify mixtures as solutions or suspensions from observations

notes.0: Calamine lotion is a mixture of several substances, not one compound. Think about why the bottle must be shaken before use.
notes.1: A solution is clear and nothing settles. Calamine lotion is cloudy. Think about why the bottle must be shaken before use.

why.right: Calamine lotion is a suspension because its insoluble particles settle at the bottom when left to stand.
wrong: Calamine lotion is a suspension because its particles are dissolved completely in the liquid.
Calamine lotion is a suspension because it is pink, and every coloured liquid is a suspension.

questions.q: Is muddy water a solution or a suspension?
questions.explain: Muddy water is cloudy, and the soil particles settle at the bottom when it is left to stand. So muddy water is a suspension.
questions.lo: Classify mixtures as solutions or suspensions from observations

notes.0: Muddy water is soil mixed with water, not a single compound. Think about what happens to the soil when it is left to stand.
notes.2: A solution is clear and nothing settles. Think about what happens to the soil in muddy water when it is left to stand.

why.right: Muddy water is a suspension because the soil particles do not dissolve and settle when left to stand.
wrong: Muddy water is a suspension because the soil dissolves completely and turns the water brown.
Muddy water is a suspension because soil and water react to form a brown compound.

questions.q: Which is observed in a suspension?
choices: solid deposits settle at the bottom
questions.explain: A suspension contains insoluble particles. These particles settle as solid deposits at the bottom when the mixture is left to stand.
questions.lo: Classify mixtures as solutions or suspensions from observations

notes.0: Particles that cannot be seen are a sign of a solution. Think about what happens to insoluble particles over time.
notes.1: Light passing through fully is a sign of a solution. A suspension is cloudy. Think about what happens to insoluble particles over time.
notes.2: A clear liquid is a sign of a solution. A suspension is cloudy. Think about what happens to insoluble particles over time.

why.right: Deposits form in a suspension because its insoluble particles are large enough to sink when left to stand.
wrong: Deposits form in a suspension because its dissolved particles react with the solvent to form a solid.
Deposits form in a suspension because the solvent evaporates quickly and leaves the solute behind.

questions.q: Which process removes insoluble substances from a suspension?
questions.explain: Filtration separates insoluble solids from a liquid. The filter paper traps the solid particles and lets the liquid pass through.
questions.lo: Classify mixtures as solutions or suspensions from observations

notes.1: Heating removes the liquid by evaporation and leaves everything else behind. Think about a method that traps only the solid particles.
notes.2: Stirring mixes the suspension again and spreads the particles through the liquid. Think about a method that traps the solid particles.
notes.3: Insoluble substances do not dissolve, so dissolving cannot remove them. Think about a method that traps the solid particles.

why.right: Filtration removes insoluble solids because the solid particles are too large to pass through the filter paper.
wrong: Filtration removes insoluble solids because the filter paper dissolves the solid particles as they pass.
Filtration removes insoluble solids because the filter paper heats the mixture and evaporates the solids.

questions.q: Which type of matter is formed by a physical change?
questions.explain: A mixture is formed when substances are mixed without a chemical reaction. This is a physical change, so no new substance is made.
questions.lo: Distinguish elements, compounds and mixtures by their characteristics

notes.0: A compound is formed in a chemical reaction, where a new substance is made. Think about what forms when substances are only mixed.
notes.1: Elements are the basic building blocks and are not made by mixing. Think about what forms when substances are only mixed.

why.right: A mixture forms in a physical change because the substances are mixed without forming a new substance.
wrong: A mixture forms in a physical change because the substances react to form a new substance.
A mixture forms in a physical change because its constituents join in a fixed proportion.

questions.q: Which type of matter is formed by a chemical reaction?
questions.explain: A compound is formed when two or more elements react and chemically combine. The new substance has different properties from its elements.
questions.lo: Distinguish elements, compounds and mixtures by their characteristics

notes.1: A mixture is formed by physical mixing, with no chemical reaction. Think about what forms when elements chemically combine.
notes.2: An element is the simplest substance. Think about what forms when two or more elements react together.

why.right: A compound forms in a chemical reaction because its elements chemically combine to make a new substance.
wrong: A compound forms in a chemical reaction because its elements are mixed but keep their own properties.
A compound forms in a chemical reaction because heating always joins substances in any proportion.

questions.q: A substance has a fixed proportion of constituents that are hard to separate. It is a
questions.explain: A compound has its elements in a fixed proportion, and they are chemically combined. This makes them hard to separate.
questions.lo: Distinguish elements, compounds and mixtures by their characteristics

notes.0: An element is only one substance, so it has no constituents to separate. Think about which type of matter has elements joined in a fixed ratio.
notes.2: A mixture can have its constituents in any proportion, and they are easy to separate. Think about which type of matter is the opposite.

why.right: A compound is hard to separate because its elements are chemically combined in a fixed proportion.
wrong: A compound is hard to separate because its elements are physically mixed in any proportion.
A compound is hard to separate because it is only one element that cannot be broken down.

questions.q: A substance keeps the properties of its constituents, which are easily separated. It is a
questions.explain: In a mixture, the constituents are not chemically combined. So they keep their own properties and can be separated easily by physical methods.
questions.lo: Distinguish elements, compounds and mixtures by their characteristics

notes.0: An element is a single substance, so it has no constituents to separate. Think about matter whose parts are not chemically combined.
notes.2: A compound has new properties, and its elements are hard to separate. Think about matter whose parts are not chemically combined.

why.right: A mixture is easy to separate because its constituents are only mixed and not chemically combined.
wrong: A mixture is easy to separate because its constituents are joined in a fixed proportion.
A mixture is easy to separate because it is made of only one type of atom.

questions.q: A substance cannot be broken down into simpler substances. Which type of matter is it?
questions.explain: An element cannot be broken down into simpler substances. This is what makes elements the basic building blocks of matter.
questions.lo: Distinguish elements, compounds and mixtures by their characteristics

notes.0: A compound can be broken down into its elements by a chemical reaction. Think about the simplest type of matter.
notes.1: A mixture can be separated into its constituents. Think about the simplest type of matter.

why.right: A substance that cannot be broken down is an element because it contains only one type of atom.
wrong: A substance that cannot be broken down is an element because its constituents are chemically combined.
A substance that cannot be broken down is an element because elements are always hard solids that cannot be cut.

questions.q: Is aluminium an element, a compound or a mixture?
questions.explain: Aluminium has one symbol, Al, in the Periodic Table. It is an element and cannot be broken down into simpler substances.
questions.lo: Classify substances as elements, compounds or mixtures

notes.1: A compound has two or more elements chemically combined. Aluminium is a single substance listed in the Periodic Table.
notes.2: A mixture contains two or more substances not chemically combined. Aluminium is a single substance listed in the Periodic Table.

why.right: Aluminium is an element because it is made of only one type of atom.
wrong: Aluminium is an element because it is a metal used to make drink cans.
Aluminium is an element because it is a mixture of metals melted together.

questions.q: Is carbon dioxide an element, a compound or a mixture?
questions.explain: Carbon dioxide is made of carbon and oxygen chemically combined in a fixed proportion. So it is a compound.
questions.lo: Classify substances as elements, compounds or mixtures

notes.1: Carbon dioxide contains two elements, carbon and oxygen, so it is not a single element. Think about how the two are joined.
notes.2: The carbon and oxygen in carbon dioxide cannot be separated by physical methods, and their proportion never changes. Think about what that shows.

why.right: Carbon dioxide is a compound because carbon and oxygen are chemically combined in a fixed proportion.
wrong: Carbon dioxide is a compound because carbon and oxygen are mixed in any proportion.
Carbon dioxide is a compound because it is a gas, and every gas is a compound.

questions.q: Is air an element, a compound or a mixture?
questions.explain: Air contains nitrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide and other gases that are not chemically combined. Their amounts can vary, so air is a mixture.
questions.lo: Classify substances as elements, compounds or mixtures

notes.0: The gases in air are not chemically combined, and their amounts vary. A compound has a fixed proportion. Think about what that means for air.
notes.2: Air contains several different gases, so it is not one element. Think about how those gases are held together.

why.right: Air is a mixture because its gases are not chemically combined and their amounts can vary.
wrong: Air is a mixture because its gases are chemically combined in a fixed proportion.
Air is a mixture because it is made up of only one type of gas, nitrogen.

questions.q: Is baking soda (sodium hydrogencarbonate) an element, a compound or a mixture?
questions.explain: Sodium hydrogencarbonate is made of sodium, hydrogen, carbon and oxygen chemically combined. So baking soda is a compound.
questions.lo: Classify substances as elements, compounds or mixtures

notes.0: The name sodium hydrogencarbonate contains several elements, so it is not a single element. Think about how they are joined.
notes.1: Baking soda is one substance with a fixed make-up, so it is not a mixture. Look at the elements named in sodium hydrogencarbonate.

why.right: Baking soda is a compound because sodium, hydrogen, carbon and oxygen are chemically combined in it.
wrong: Baking soda is a compound because it is a white powder, and every powder is a compound.
Baking soda is a compound because its elements are mixed in any proportion.

questions.q: Is milk an element, a compound or a mixture?
questions.explain: Milk contains water, fat, protein, sugar and other substances that are not chemically combined. So milk is a mixture.
questions.lo: Classify substances as elements, compounds or mixtures

notes.0: Milk contains many different substances, so it is not one element. Think about whether those substances are chemically combined.
notes.1: Milk is made of many substances, such as water and fat, that are not chemically combined. A compound is a single substance with a fixed make-up.

why.right: Milk is a mixture because it contains several substances, such as water and fat, not chemically combined.
wrong: Milk is a mixture because its substances are chemically combined in a fixed proportion.
Milk is a mixture because it comes from an animal, and only man-made substances are compounds.

questions.q: Which substance is a compound?
questions.explain: Water is made of hydrogen and oxygen chemically combined, so it is a compound. Oxygen is an element, and steel and air are mixtures.
questions.lo: Classify substances as elements, compounds or mixtures

notes.0: Oxygen has one symbol, O, in the Periodic Table, so it is an element. Look for a substance with elements chemically combined.
notes.1: Steel is a mixture of iron, carbon and other elements. Look for a substance with elements chemically combined.
notes.2: Air is a mixture of gases that are not chemically combined. Look for a substance with elements chemically combined.

why.right: Water is a compound because hydrogen and oxygen are chemically combined in it in a fixed proportion.
wrong: Water is a compound because it is a liquid, and every liquid is a compound.
Water is a compound because hydrogen and oxygen are mixed in it in any proportion.
